checks.name: b.ac_why
checks.q: For each acceptance criterion in the brief (a done-evidence item, threshold, gate or success condition), does the text say why it is a criterion, i.e. what failure or risk it guards against?
levels: No reasons given for any criterion
Every criterion states what it guards against
checks.basis: U2 (Cody): agents treat a stated criterion as binding authority; the reason it exists decides whether a breach is a stop or a flag.

checks.name: b.ac_proven_required
checks.q: For each acceptance criterion in the brief, does the text show how it is known to be required (a measurement, an upstream requirement, or a stated derivation) with a pointer that could be checked (command and date, document and section, or the inputs it derives from)?
levels: Every criterion has a checkable pointer, or is labelled as a judgement
checks.basis: U2: acceptance criteria are end-of-chain outputs; one with no provenance marks the research and direction above it as unjustified, forcing the backward audit.

checks.name: b.ac_judgement_labelled
checks.q: Where an acceptance criterion or number in the brief is a judgement or an estimate rather than measured or derived, is it labelled as such (so a worker can treat a breach as advisory), instead of being presented as a hard requirement?
levels: Judgement calls are presented as hard requirements
All judgement calls are labelled, or none exist
checks.basis: U2: '10k' and '10k because it feels about right' trigger different agent behaviour; the label is what makes the difference.
